LeagueGuide.title: League Mode
LeagueGuide.summary: The parties of the highest-scoring League players become the Elite Four and Champion for the next challenger.
LeagueGuide.starterBody: Pick one Pokémon from this season’s starter lineup.
LeagueGuide.growthTitle: Build your party in the League field
LeagueGuide.growthBody: Battle and catch wild Pokémon in the League’s own field. You can’t transfer parties between League and multiplayer.
LeagueGuide.badgeTitle: Find the Gym Leaders and earn badges
LeagueGuide.badgeBody: Defeat eight Gym Leaders in order to collect eight badges. The next Gym Leader appears at a random spot in the field, walks around, and eventually leaves. When the notice appears, use the area and direction shown above the field to find them. If you lose, you keep the badges you’ve already earned.
LeagueGuide.entryTitle: Enter with a party of six
LeagueGuide.entryBody: Entry uses up your badges and eligibility. Your party starts fully recovered.
LeagueGuide.battleTitle: Face the Elite Four and Champion
LeagueGuide.battleBody: Take on the four Elite Four members and then the Champion. A loss ends the attempt without a record. You keep your training progress, then collect the badges again to start with the first opponent.
LeagueGuide.levelBody: Pokémon above level 50 are scaled down to level 50 for League battles.
LeagueGuide.itemsBody: NPC Gym Leaders and the initial Elite Four and Champion can use their original held items. Challengers and registered defense parties battle without held items.
LeagueGuide.recoveryBody: Conscious Pokémon recover half their missing HP and PP, rounded up, and clear any status conditions. Fainted Pokémon stay fainted for the rest of the attempt.
LeagueGuide.scoringTitle: Match scores and the final score
LeagueGuide.scoringBody: A win is worth up to 100 points: 55 based on how many Pokémon fainted that match, 15 for the average HP percentage of surviving Pokémon, and 30 for turn efficiency. The average of all five matches counts for 80% and the average of the two lowest counts for 20%. The result is scaled to 10,000 points.
LeagueGuide.rankingBody: Each player has one ranked record per season, their personal best. Ties go to the earlier record. First place becomes Champion, and places two through five make up the Elite Four.
LeagueGuide.defenseBody: The record keeps the party as it was when you completed the run. AI controls registered parties, fully recovered for every challenger. After completing a run, you choose a new starter for your next attempt.
LeagueGuide.npcBody: At the start of a season, Will, Koga, Bruno, Karen, and Champion Lance from Pokémon HeartGold fill the five positions.
LeagueGuide.seasonBody: Pre-league has no closing date or season settlement. Play as a guest or sign in with Discord. Guests can get a resume code in the account menu to continue the same progress on another device.
LeagueGuide.officialBody: Pre-league records reset when the official season starts. Official seasons last four weeks and require Discord sign-in.
